SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Time, Distance and Speed, part of MEASUREMENTS 3.3 Mass, Volume, Weight and Density (8 Lessons) By the end of the  in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9 GRADE.

Key inquiry question: How do we observe speed in daily activities? 2. Why does time vary in different places of the world?

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Time, Distance and Speed together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking and problem solving: Completes tasks by following instruction; A learner describes the procedure to be

followed when measuring distances and time, for example running track events to determine speed

● Creativity and imagination: Imagines different situations; A learner studies the instructions before working out and relate

time of different places on the earth

Values:
● Integrity: A learner enhances discipline as they correctly record individual running time during track events and other

games.

● Respect: A learner enhances etiquette as they adhere to their lanes on track events and other games.

35

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
● Safety and security: A learner observes safety measures and time during games and sports.

● Education for Sustainable Development (ESD): A learner participates and chooses careers in games and sporting

activities.

● Self-awareness: A learner participates and times themselves in games.

Link to other learning areas:

● Integrated Science: A learner uses digital devices to tell time in different zones of the world.

Suggested learning Resources:

digital devices, maps, globes, digital clocks.
